AI.tldr: 2D feature-evolution analysis in ViTs across layers and epochs using Sparse Autoencoders to track sparse CLS-feature activations, revealing early feature migration and stronger stabilization in deeper layers.
AI.motivation: Understand feature-level learning dynamics in Vision Transformers beyond representation-level similarity by tracking how individual features migrate across layers during training.
AI.method: Train ViTs; extract CLS-token representations; use Sparse Autoencoders to learn sparse feature candidates; compare their activation profiles across epoch–layer pairs to identify feature-level dynamics and migration.
AI.result: Feature migration is concentrated early in training, occurs more often toward earlier layers than deeper ones, and diminishes as features stabilize. Deeper layers stabilize earlier and more strongly than shallow layers.
AI.conclusion: The proposed framework provides a tool to analyze ViT learning dynamics and feature evolution, offering insight into how features organize and migrate during training.

title: Electronic Navigational Chart Change Classification
summary: Electronic Navigational Charts (ENCs) are geospatial vector datasets used in maritime navigation systems that represent hydrographic and navigational information such as depths, navigational aids, traffic schemes, and hazards. A major challenge for hydrographic offices is determining whether a given chart change poses a critical or non-critical risk to maritime safety. Existing workflows rely heavily on manual review and verification, which is labor-intensive, scales poorly with the volume of incoming chart updates, and introduces inter-analyst inconsistencies. To address this challenge, we propose a method for automated classification of ENC changes. We establish a baseline encoding scheme to translate complex vector data changes into a structured tabular format for classification models. The two crucial components of the encoding scheme include a spatial context encoder to enrich the change representations with surrounding geographic features, and an ENC attribute encoder to represent nuanced attribute-value descriptions of the modified objects. We evaluate the proposed approach across two distinct operational datasets, comprising 1,308 chart pairs containing over 100,000 individual chart modifications. Tuned gradient-boosted trees leveraging the proposed encoding schemes achieve accuracies of 90% and 94% on the two datasets, yielding a 5-7% improvement over default hyperparameterized models trained on encodings without spatial context and attribute embeddings. These results demonstrate the viability of integrating machine learning into operational geospatial pipelines to improve ENC maintenance and enhance maritime safety. Finally, our experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of simple location and spatial aggregation methods, providing a foundation for evaluating more sophisticated spatial representation learning techniques for this application.

AI.tldr: Proposes an automated ENC-change classifier using a spatial-context encoder and an ENC-attribute encoder; achieves 90-94% accuracy on two real-world datasets, outperforming encodings without context by 5-7%.
AI.motivation: Manual chart-change review is labor-intensive, scales poorly with update volume, and introduces inter-analyst inconsistencies. An automated classification framework can improve efficiency, consistency, and maritime safety.
AI.method: Baseline encoding that translates complex vector changes into a structured tabular format. Introduces a spatial context encoder to enrich change representations with surrounding geographic features and an ENC attribute encoder to capture nuanced attribute-value descriptions of modified objects. Evaluated with tuned gradient-boosted trees on two operational datasets (1,308 chart pairs; >100k modifications). Compared against encodings without spatial context/attribute embeddings.
AI.result: Accuracies of 90% and 94% on the two datasets. 5-7% improvement over default hyperparameterized models trained on encodings without spatial context and attribute embeddings. Simple location and spatial aggregation methods demonstrated effectiveness, suggesting a solid foundation for exploring more sophisticated spatial representation learning techniques.
AI.conclusion: demonstrates viability of integrating ML into operational geospatial pipelines for ENC maintenance and maritime safety. Encourages further work on advanced spatial representation learning while validating practical gains in real-world settings.

title: SAE-Xplainers: Rule-Based Feature Interpretation for Extreme Earth Events
comment: 22 pages, 16 Figures, Under Review. A non-archival 2-page version was accepted as an oral presentation at Climate Informatics 2026 (Extended Abstract ID 66, https://github.com/freddy0218/ClimateInformatics2026/tree/main), and a non-archival 4-page version was accepted as an oral presentation at the AICC Workshop at ECCV 2026
summary: The emergence of large-scale Weather and Climate (W&C) datasets offers new opportunities for modeling extreme Earth events (ExEE) and their impacts using deep learning. However, their adoption in operational settings remains limited by the lack of models' interpretability. While for conventional text and image modalities, tools such as Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) have proven effective for extracting human-understandable concepts, their use for the analysis of ExEE remains challenging due to the nature of W&C data. To address this, we introduce (i) a geographic location-based modulation of the inputs of SAE to capture the local semantic meaning of environmental patterns, and (ii) an ensemble of rule-based SAE-Xplainers to interpret the resulting high-dimensional features derived from complex, multi-modal environmental predictors. We evaluate our method on three ExEE types: the prediction of fires, and the detection of tropical cyclones and atmospheric rivers. We show that SAE input modulation improves both reconstruction performance and feature utilization, and that our SAE-Xplainers enable faithful interpretation of complex climatic patterns by unfolding them into human-understandable rules that are consistent with the scientific literature, while also supporting the identification of feature absorption.

AI.tldr: SAE with geographic input modulation and SAE-Xplainers for ExEE in W&C; improves reconstruction and produces interpretable, literature-consistent rules across fires, tropical cyclones, and atmospheric rivers.
AI.motivation: Increase interpretability of deep learning models for large-scale Weather & Climate data and their extreme events, by extracting human-understandable concepts and rules.
AI.method: Introduce location-based modulation of sparse autoencoder inputs to capture local semantics; develop an ensemble of rule-based SAE-Xplainers to translate high-dimensional features into human-readable rules derived from multi-modal environmental predictors; evaluate on three ExEE tasks (fire prediction, tropical cyclone detection, atmospheric river detection).
AI.result: Input modulation improves reconstruction quality and feature utilization; SAE-Xplainers provide faithful, rule-based interpretations that unfold complex patterns into human-understandable rules, consistent with the scientific literature and capable of revealing feature absorption.
AI.conclusion: The approach enhances DL model interpretability for ExEE in W&C, offering actionable insights aligned with domain knowledge and potentially aiding operational adoption by exposing transparent, rule-based explanations.

title: DPC-Net: Dual-Prior Collaborative Network for All-in-One Image Restoration
summary: All-in-One Image Restoration (AiOIR) aims to handle diverse degradations within a unified model. However, existing methods often overlook image semantics in degradation modeling and lack low-level visual priors during reconstruction, leading to structural distortions and semantic inconsistencies. To address these issues, we propose a novel Dual-Prior Collaborative Network (DPC-Net), which achieves high-quality restoration by jointly exploiting degradation-semantic coupled priors and low-level visual priors. Specifically, degraded images are fed into a Degradation-Aware Network (DAN) to extract degradation-semantic coupled features. To this end, a Vision-Language Model (VLM) supervises DAN by constraining its features distribution, introducing image semantics into the encoding of degradation patterns. A Degradation-Semantic Modulation Module (DSMM) further translates this guidance into degradation-semantic coupling and propagates coupled representations to the decoder. During decoding, knowledge bases provide low-level visual priors, and the Dual-Prior Collaborative Reconstruction Module (DPCR) integrates dual-prior information to guide degradation removal while preserving structure and semantics, producing high-fidelity restored images. Extensive experiments on multiple restoration benchmarks demonstrate that DPC-Net achieves superior performance against state-of-the-art AiOIR methods.

AI.tldr: DPC-Net integrates degradation-semantic priors and low-level visual priors to improve all-in-one image restoration, using a degradation-aware encoder supervised by a vision-language model and a dual-prior reconstruction module that fuses semantic and structural cues via knowledge bases.
AI.motivation: AiOIR methods often ignore the semantic structure of degraded content and lack explicit low-level priors, leading to distortions and semantic inconsistencies during restoration.
AI.method: Propose DPC-Net comprising: (1) Degradation-Aware Network (DAN) to extract degradation-semantic coupled features; (2) Vision-Language Model (VLM) supervision to constrain DAN’s feature distribution, injecting image semantics into degradation pattern encoding; (3) Degradation-Semantic Modulation Module (DSMM) translating guidance into coupled representations; (4) knowledge-base informed decoding with low-level priors; (5) Dual-Prior Collaborative Reconstruction Module (DPCR) to integrate dual-prior information for restoration.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on multiple restoration benchmarks show that DPC-Net achieves superior performance compared with state-of-the-art AiOIR methods.
AI.conclusion: The proposed dual-prior framework effectively leverages degradation-semantic coupling and low-level priors to produce high-fidelity restorations, setting a new direction for unified image restoration.

title: InsufficiencyBench: Evaluating LLM legal advice on underspecified user queries
comment: 10 pages, Best Paper Honorable Mention at ICML AI4Law 2026
summary: Legal AI systems are increasingly used to answer legal questions, yet existing benchmarks assume queries arrive fully specified. In practice, users omit facts that materially determine the legal outcome. We introduce InsufficiencyBench, the first legal benchmark targeting query-side insufficiency: whether a model recognizes when a query lacks legally material information, identifies what is missing, and refrains from premature conclusions. We formalize a taxonomy of eight canonical missing-element categories across three structural failure modes---switch, gating, and fatal prerequisite--- and construct 202 benchmark items (58 base queries, 144 deficient variants) spanning six legal domains and 24 US jurisdictions and annotated by practising attorneys. Evaluating ten frontier models, we find that no model exceeds F2 = 0.46 on missing-element identification and that the median recall is 0.44. Models either hedge indiscriminately or answer silently under fabricated presumptions. No model both identifies and qualifies responses to deficient queries while directly addressing complete ones.

AI.tldr: InsufficiencyBench: a legal AI benchmark for query-side insufficiency; assesses whether models detect under-specified queries, identify what's missing, and avoid premature conclusions; current models underperform.
AI.motivation: Real-world legal queries are often underspecified; existing benchmarks assume complete information, risking incorrect outcomes; measure model's recognition and handling of missing material facts.
AI.method: Formal taxonomy of eight missing-element categories across three structural failure modes (switch, gating, fatal prerequisite); 202 benchmark items (58 base, 144 deficient variants); spans six domains and 24 US jurisdictions; benchmark annotated by practicing attorneys; evaluation on ten frontier models.
AI.result: No model exceeds F2 = 0.46 for missing-element identification; median recall 0.44; models hedge or answer silently under presumptions; none both identify and address complete vs deficient queries.
AI.conclusion: Current models struggle to detect insufficiency and to refrain from premature or fabricated conclusions; indicates substantial gap in safe, reliable legal AI; calls for methods to detect missing information, calibrate uncertainty, and handle incomplete queries.

title: Evaluating Neural Cartographic Relief Shading for Urban Environments: A Downtown Calgary Study Using High-Resolution DEM and DSM Data
summary: This article explores the performance of analytical and neural-based hillshading methods in a dense urban environment using high-resolution digital elevation model (DEM) and digital surface model (DSM) data for downtown Calgary. The study compares single-direction and multi-direction analytical hillshading with relief shading generated in Eduard, a machine-learning system originally developed to emulate Swiss-style shaded relief trained primarily on mountainous landscapes. Because Eduard was not designed for buildings, bridges, streets, trees, and other urban infrastructures, the central question is not whether it perfectly reproduces urban morphology, but whether parameter tuning can nevertheless produce visually strong, cartographically useful, and in some cases superior results when compared with conventional analytical methods. The analysis focuses especially on terrain type, micro and macro generalization, and flat-area detail parameters, while keeping the large-scale shading style constant throughout the neural experiments. The article is structured as an exploratory comparison rather than a benchmark of universal best practice. It aims to identify where analytical hillshading remains more reliable, where Eduard offers unexpected strengths, and where neural shading fails because of its training bias toward alpine terrain. The study contributes to current work on terrain representation by testing whether a neural approach designed for natural landforms can be adapted to a highly built urban setting, and it concludes by arguing for future model training and evaluation specifically targeted at urban relief shading.

AI.tldr: A comparative study evaluating analytical and neural-based hillshading in downtown Calgary using high-resolution DEM/DSM. It analyzes whether tuning a mountainous-terrain–oriented neural system (Eduard) can produce useful urban relief shading and where it excels or fails relative to conventional analytical hillshading; it advocates urban-focused training.
AI.motivation: Assess if a neural shading model trained on natural terrain can be effectively adapted to dense urban relief shading and how it compares with classical analytical methods for cartographic quality.
AI.method: Experiment compares single-direction and multi-direction analytical hillshading with neural-generated relief shading from Eduard, using city-scale high-resolution DEM/DSM for downtown Calgary. Large-scale shading style is held constant across neural experiments. The study emphasizes terrain type, micro/macro generalization, and flat-area detail, adopting an exploratory, not benchmarking, design.
AI.result: Findings suggest parameter tuning can yield visually strong, and sometimes superior, results versus conventional analyses in urban contexts. Eduard exhibits unexpected strengths, but neural shading may falter due to training bias toward alpine terrain. The study demonstrates that a neural model designed for natural landforms can be adapted to urban relief shading but requires targeted urban-focused training and evaluation.
AI.conclusion: Neural approaches for natural terrains can be adapted to urban relief shading with urban-targeted training and evaluation; future work should center on urban-specific data and metrics for model development and assessment.

title: PelviNeXt: A Modality-Agnostic Hybrid Network for Pelvic Imaging in Women's Health
summary: Women's health remains substantially under-resourced in medical imaging research, with pelvic pathologies such as polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) and pelvic fracture both suffering from a scarcity of public, well-annotated benchmark data despite their clinical importance. We introduce PelviNeXt, a modality-agnostic hybrid architecture combining a dense convolutional feature extractor, hierarchical channel-spatial attention (H-CBAM), a multi-scale fusion module (MSFM), and talking-heads multi-head self-attention (TH-MHSA), applied without modification to both pelvic ultrasound and X-ray inputs. While benchmarking PelviNeXt on PCOSGen, the only gynaecologist-annotated public PCOS ultrasound dataset, we identified extensive exact and near-duplicate contamination within and across the dataset. We audit this contamination via perceptual hashing, publicly release a deduplicated version of the dataset, and establish the first integrity-audited evaluation protocol and baseline for PCOSGen under 5-fold cross-validation. On the only publicly available pelvic fracture X-ray dataset (PXR150), PelviNeXt exceeds previously reported state-of-the-art results across accuracy, recall, specificity, and AUROC. Ablation studies confirm that each architectural component contributes to performance on both tasks. Our results demonstrate that a single architecture, applied without task-specific modification, can serve as a reliable foundation for pelvic imaging across modalities in data-scarce, under-researched areas of women's health.

AI.tldr: PelviNeXt is a modality-agnostic pelvic-imaging model that delivers SOTA results on pelvic fracture X-rays and sets a cleaned, integrity-aware baseline for PCOS ultrasound, highlighting data quality and cross-modality transfer in data-scarce settings.
AI.motivation: Women's pelvic imaging (PCOS ultrasound and pelvic fracture X-ray) is data-scarce and under-resourced; public, well-annotated benchmarks are scarce, hindering AI progress and clinical translation.
AI.method: PelviNeXt is a modality-agnostic hybrid architecture comprising a dense convolutional feature extractor, hierarchical channel-spatial attention (H-CBAM), a multi-scale fusion module (MSFM), and talking-heads multi-head self-attention (TH-MHSA). It is applied without task-specific modification to ultrasound and X-ray inputs. The study audits data contamination in PCOSGen using perceptual hashing, releases a deduplicated PCOSGen, and evaluates with a 5-fold cross-validation baseline. It benchmarks on PXR150 (pelvic fracture X-ray) and conducts ablations to verify component contributions.
AI.result: On PXR150, PelviNeXt surpasses previously reported state-of-the-art across accuracy, recall, specificity, and AUROC. For PCOSGen, a deduplicated, integrity-audited version is released and a first robust evaluation baseline under 5-fold CV is established. Ablation shows all architectural components contribute to performance on both tasks.
AI.conclusion: A single, task-agnostic architecture can serve as a reliable foundation for pelvic imaging across modalities in data-scarce women's health domains, with explicit data integrity practices enhancing evaluative credibility.

title: Rule-Compliant Visual Spatial Planning for Multimodal Large Language Models
summary: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) combine linguistic reasoning with visual perception, yet their ability to perform visual spatial planning under explicit or previously unseen rule constraints remains underexplored. This setting requires models to jointly understand spatial layouts, interpret natural-language rules, and plan valid actions accordingly. To address this gap, we introduce RuleMaze, a controllable benchmark in which MLLMs must navigate mazes while obeying natural-language rules of varying complexity. RuleMaze isolates rule-compliant spatial planning by requiring accurate perception, rule interpretation, and constrained action planning. To enable scalable and systematic rule construction, we propose Language-Logic-Function Hybridization, which automatically generates natural-language rules and translates them into logical representations and executable validators, eliminating manual rule engineering. To improve rule following and generalization, we introduce Disentangled Multimodal Planning (DMP), which separates perception, execution, and rule verification through interpretable reasoning primitives. By disentangling these components, DMP facilitates systematic generalization to more complex and previously unseen rules, while providing transparent intermediate planning traces. Experiments demonstrate that DMP substantially improves rule compliance and planning success compared to end-to-end textual planning baselines. Overall, RuleMaze establishes a principled benchmark for studying grounded and interpretable rule-based spatial planning in MLLMs. Code is available at https://github.com/oceanflowlab/RuleMaze.

AI.tldr: A new benchmark, RuleMaze, evaluates multimodal LLMs on rule-constrained visual-spatial planning and introduces two methods—Language-Logic-Function Hybridization and Disentangled Multimodal Planning (DMP)—to improve rule compliance, generalization, and transparent reasoning; experiments show DMP outperforms end-to-end baselines, and code is released.
AI.motivation: To study how multimodal LLMs perform spatial planning under explicit and unseen natural-language rule constraints, addressing the gap where perception, rule interpretation, and constrained action planning are jointly required but underexplored.
AI.method: RuleMaze provides controllable mazes with natural-language rules; Language-Logic-Function Hybridization automatically generates natural-language rules and translates them into logical representations and executable validators; Disentangled Multimodal Planning decomposes the pipeline into perception, execution, and rule verification using interpretable reasoning primitives to enable generalization and transparent traces.
AI.result: DMP substantially improves rule compliance and planning success relative to end-to-end textual planning baselines, and RuleMaze offers a principled benchmark for grounded, interpretable rule-based spatial planning in MLLMs.
AI.conclusion: RuleMaze enables principled study of rule-based spatial planning in MLLMs; the proposed hybridization and disentangled planning approach enhances generalization to complex/unseen rules and provides transparent planning traces; code is publicly available.

title: Ask Self, Ask Others: Relation Is All You Need
summary: Attention directly derives normalized information flow from pairwise scores. We introduce Relation, an alternative token-mixing primitive that first organizes pairwise evidence into explicit Self and Exchange relations and derives information flow afterward. This relational organization gives rise to Full Relation, FlashRelation, Linear Relation, Hybrid Relation, and a KV-style Relation Cache. Across matched decoder-only models at approximately 10M, 30M, and 100M parameters, Full Relation achieves lower final validation NLL than MHA at all three scales. In a fixed-context reference benchmark, FlashRelation is 3.60-4.41x faster than the materialized Full Relation implementation. Across scale-matched production workloads, it reaches 76.4-84.9% of PyTorch FlashAttention throughput while executing the Full Relation operator. Hybrid Relation uses 75% Linear Relation layers and achieves strong language-modeling quality. These results support a relation-first view of token mixing: ask Self, ask Others, then let Flow follow Relation.

AI.tldr: Proposes a relation-based token-mixing primitive that replaces/augments self-attention with explicit Self and Exchange relations, yielding several variants (Full, Flash, Linear, Hybrid, KV-Cache) and showing improved language modeling performance and efficiency over MHA at multiple scales.
AI.motivation: To organize pairwise evidences into explicit relational components before deriving information flow, enabling more efficient and potentially higher-quality token mixing than traditional multi-head attention (MHA).
AI.method: Introduce relation-based primitives: Self and Exchange relations leading to Full Relation, FlashRelation, Linear Relation, Hybrid Relation, and a KV-style Relation Cache. Evaluate on decoder-only models at ~10M/30M/100M params; assess in fixed-context benchmarks and production workloads; compare against MHA and FlashAttention.
AI.result: Full Relation achieves lower final validation NLL than MHA across scales (10M, 30M, 100M). FlashRelation is 3.60–4.41× faster than the materialized Full Relation in fixed-context benchmarks. Across production workloads, Full Relation reaches ~76.4–84.9% of PyTorch FlashAttention throughput. Hybrid Relation uses 75% Linear Relation layers while maintaining strong LMs. The results support a relation-first view: ask Self, ask Others, then Flow follow Relation.
AI.conclusion: A relation-first paradigm for token mixing can outperform traditional MHA in language modeling quality and offer substantial efficiency gains, with multiple variants to balance speed and quality.

title: Artificial Intelligence for Workflow Analysis in Colorectal Surgery: A Multicentric, Cross-Procedural Development and Generalization Study
summary: Minimally invasive colorectal surgeries (MIS-CRS) are characterised by significant variability and inconsistent outcomes. ColoWorkflow, a tool for the video-based assessment (VBA) of MIS-CRS workflow, was recently validated. However, manual VBA is time-consuming, limiting implementation. This study presents AI-ColoWorkflow, a deep learning model for automated surgical workflow analysis across MIS-CRS. Operative videos of MIS-CRS were collected from 4 centres and a publicly available dataset. Phases and steps were manually annotated according to ColoWorkflow. A deep learning model combining a fine-tuned DINOv3 vision transformer for per-frame visual feature extraction with a hierarchical multi-stage temporal convolutional network was jointly optimized for phase and step recognition. The model trained on pooled multicentric data, namely AI-ColoWorkflow was compared against centre-specific and procedure-specific models on a held-out test set. The following metrics were used for evaluation: macro F1 score, balanced accuracy, precision, and recall. AI-ColoWorkflow achieved a macro F1 of 73.01% $\pm$ 10.27 (balanced accuracy 73.43%) for phase recognition and 39.82% $\pm$ 7.06 (balanced accuracy 38.65%) for step recognition. The global model outperformed centre- and procedure-specific models in most experiments except procedure-specific step recognition. In the generalization analysis, mean F1 was 48.42% for phase recognition. AI-ColoWorkflow can reliably recognize MIS-CRS phases. A single model trained on pooled, multicentric, multi-procedural data generalises at least as well as and often better than centre- or procedure-specific models for phase recognition in MIS-CRS, while procedure-specific step models retain advantages for certain procedure types, motivating hybrid training strategies for future surgical AI development.

AI.tldr: A deep learning model (AI-ColoWorkflow) combines DINOv3 features with a hierarchical TCN to automate MIS-CRS workflow analysis (phase/step) across multicenter data; macro F1 ~73% for phase and ~40% for step; pooled multicenter data improves phase generalization; center-/procedure-specific step models offer advantages for some procedures; suggests hybrid training strategies.
AI.motivation: Reduce reliance on time-consuming manual video-based assessment (VBA) of MIS-CRS and address variability in outcomes by enabling automated, scalable workflow analysis across multiple centers and procedures.
AI.method: Data from 4 centers plus a public dataset; manual annotation of phases and steps per ColoWorkflow; architecture combines a fine-tuned DINOv3 vision transformer for per-frame features with a hierarchical multi-stage temporal convolutional network for phase and step recognition; trained on pooled multicentric data; compared against centre-specific and procedure-specific models on a held-out test set; evaluated with macro F1, balanced accuracy, precision, and recall; generalization assessed across centers/procedures.
AI.result: Phase recognition: macro F1 73.01% ± 10.27; balanced accuracy 73.43%. Step recognition: macro F1 39.82% ± 7.06; balanced accuracy 38.65%. The global model generally outperformed centre- and procedure-specific models for phase recognition; procedure-specific models retained advantages for certain procedures in step recognition. Generalization (mean F1 for phase) 48.42%, indicating domain shift; AI-ColoWorkflow reliably recognizes MIS-CRS phases; a single pooled multicentric model generalizes at least as well as, and often better than, centre-/procedure-specific models for phase recognition; hybrid training strategies are motivated for future development.
AI.conclusion: A single multicentric model can effectively recognize MIS-CRS phases, with better generalization for phase recognition than center- or procedure-specific models; for steps, procedure-specific models may still be advantageous in some procedures, suggesting hybrid training approaches for future AI development in surgical workflow analysis.

title: QUASAR: A Quantum-Classical Neural Network for SAR Satellite Physical-Layer Authentication
summary: X-band SAR satellites (8-12 GHz) play a critical role in disaster response, environmental monitoring, and military intelligence. Yet, they lack robust physical-layer authentication (PLA), a security layer orthogonal to cryptographic solutions. Existing PLA systems, typically based on radio-frequency fingerprinting, are often limited to sub-6 GHz frequencies and rely on classical deep learning. However, this approach underfits the IQ phase nonlinearities that distinguish satellite hardware. In this paper, we present QUASAR, to the best of our knowledge the first quantum-classical hybrid architecture that fuses a CNN spectrogram encoder with a variational quantum circuit (VQC) to provide PLA to X-band SAR signals. Our solution enjoys two distinctive features: (i) it is markedly more data-efficient than classical machine learning, requiring only 10% of the training data to match the accuracy of classical baselines -- data collection being notoriously the most time-consuming phase of PLA; and, (ii) at an equal data budget, it improves classification accuracy over those baselines. In detail, we test our solution under three adversarial scenarios: replay, crafted-IQ injection, and space-borne spoofing. QUASAR rejects spoofed transmissions in 89.7%, 94.1%, and 81.3% of attempts, respectively, establishing the first quantum-enhanced physical-layer classifier for satellite constellations. The fully detailed framework and the supporting results, other than being interesting on their own, show a novel research avenue for physical-layer authentication.

AI.tldr: QUASAR introduces a quantum-classical hybrid PLA for X-band SAR signals, using a CNN spectrogram encoder and a variational quantum circuit to achieve data-efficient and robust physical-layer authentication for satellites, outperforming baselines under limited data.
AI.motivation: X-band SAR security is critical for disaster response, environmental monitoring, and military intelligence. Classical PLA methods rely on RF fingerprinting and need large datasets; satellite hardware IQ nonlinearities are underutilized, motivating a data-efficient, robust solution.
AI.method: A CNN-based spectrogram encoder is fused with a variational quantum circuit (VQC) to form QUASAR, a quantum-classical hybrid architecture for physical-layer authentication of X-band SAR transmissions. The system is evaluated under replay, crafted-IQ injection, and space-borne spoofing scenarios.
AI.result: With only 10% of the training data, QUASAR matches the accuracy of classical baselines; at equivalent data budgets, it achieves higher classification accuracy. Spoofing rejection rates on three attack types are 89.7% (replay), 94.1% (crafted-IQ), and 81.3% (space-borne spoofing).
AI.conclusion: QUASAR is the first quantum-enhanced physical-layer classifier for satellite constellations, highlighting a novel research avenue at the intersection of quantum computing and RF security, with data-efficiency and robustness advantages that warrant further exploration and hardware validation.

title: A Standardized Framework for Machine Learning in Power System Protection
comment: 32 pages, 4 figures, 26 tables. Code: https://github.com/julianoelhaf/protection-eval-framework. Dataset: PROTECT-90, doi:10.5281/zenodo.21109169
summary: Studies of machine-learning-based power-system protection increasingly report near-perfect scores, yet the meaning of those scores depends strongly on the evaluation setting. Protection task, physical scope, measurements, timing, targets, preprocessing, and validation often vary jointly and remain incompletely specified. This paper proposes a standardization-oriented framework that treats evaluation design as part of the scientific contribution. It defines seven required study dimensions: protection objective, physical scope, observability, timing and decision windows, targets and sample validity, validation protocol, and evaluation outputs. The framework is instantiated in a bounded case study on the public PROTECT-90 electromagnetic-transient benchmark, comprising 9022 simulated episodes from a 90 kV double-line topology, for onset-conditioned fault classification and localization. Under centralized sensing, simulation-metadata-aligned 20 ms windows, and episode-grouped validation, a multi-layer perceptron (MLP) achieved a five-fold mean macro-averaged F1 score of 0.991 +/- 0.001 for classification and a localization mean absolute error of 10.20 +/- 0.25% of line length (mean +/- std across episode-grouped folds). Extending the decision horizon to 50 ms preserved this task-dependent performance asymmetry, while reduced observability approximately doubled the MLP localization error but had little effect on classification. A synchronized two-ended conventional locator outperformed the learning locators under its richer clean information set, and measurement degradation showed that clean predictive performance did not determine robustness. The framework turns evaluation assumptions into explicit, reproducible evidence and provides a basis for more comparable, auditable evaluation and future certification-oriented assessment of machine-learning protection functions.

AI.tldr: A standardization-focused evaluation framework for ML-based power-system protection; defines seven dimensions; validated on PROTECT-90 with MLP achieving near-perfect classification and precise localization; findings show horizon and observability affect results; underscores need for comparable, auditable evaluation and certification-oriented assessment.
AI.motivation: Inconsistent evaluation setups across ML-based protection studies yield incomparable and potentially misleading performance metrics; a standardized evaluation design is needed to enable fair comparisons and pave the way for certification.
AI.method: Proposes seven required study dimensions for evaluation design (protection objective, physical scope, observability, timing/decision windows, targets/sample validity, validation protocol, evaluation outputs). Instantiates framework on PROTECT-90 EM-transient benchmark (9022 simulated episodes on a 90 kV double-line topology) for onset-conditioned fault classification and localization. Uses centralized sensing, 20 ms windows aligned with simulation metadata, and episode-grouped validation. Compares ML (MLP) with a conventional locator under different observability and horizon settings.
AI.result: MLP achieved a five-fold mean macro-averaged F1 score of 0.991 ± 0.001 for classification and a localization MAE of 10.20 ± 0.25% of line length (across episode-grouped folds). Extending decision horizon to 50 ms preserved task-dependent performance asymmetry. Reduced observability roughly doubled localization error but had little effect on classification. A synchronized two-ended conventional locator outperformed learning locators when richer clean information was available. Measurement degradation showed that clean predictive performance did not determine robustness.
AI.conclusion: The framework converts evaluation assumptions into explicit, reproducible evidence and provides a basis for more comparable, auditable evaluation and future certification-oriented assessment of ML protection functions.

title: G3Ego: Gaze-Guided Graphs for Egocentric Action Understanding
comment: Accepted at the CONTEXTUS Workshop, ECCV 2026
summary:
Egocentric action understanding is often addressed using large video models pretrained on extensive exocentric datasets. However, many first-person actions depend on a small number of hand-object interactions involving only a few relevant entities.
  We propose G3Ego, a graph-based framework for egocentric action understanding that uses gaze as a structural cue to identify action-relevant entities in the scene. From sparsely sampled frames, G3Ego constructs action scene graphs from vision-language descriptions, grounded objects, and hand cues, and then prunes irrelevant entities using the camera wearer's gaze.
  The resulting graph embeddings are temporally aggregated for action recognition and anticipation. Unlike prior work that uses gaze primarily as an auxiliary modality or attention signal, G3Ego incorporates gaze directly into graph construction, producing efficient and interpretable representations focused on action-relevant interactions.
  Experiments on EGTEA Gaze+ and MECCANO show that G3Ego achieves competitive performance compared with video-based approaches and consistently improves Macro-F1 under class-imbalanced evaluation, while avoiding reliance on computationally expensive video pretraining. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of gaze-guided graph representations for egocentric action understanding.

AI.tldr: G3Ego presents a gaze-guided, graph-based framework for egocentric action understanding that builds action scene graphs from sparse frames using vision-language cues, grounded objects, and hand cues, then prunes with gaze; temporally aggregates graph embeddings for recognition and anticipation, achieving competitive results without heavy video pretraining and improved Macro-F1 on imbalanced data.
AI.motivation: Egocentric action understanding often hinges on a small number of hand–object interactions, yet many methods rely on large exocentric pretraining or treat gaze as auxiliary. There is a need for representations that focus on action-relevant entities and are efficient and interpretable.
AI.method: From sparsely sampled frames, construct action scene graphs by fusing vision–language descriptions, grounded objects, and hand cues; apply the wearer’s gaze to prune irrelevant entities and emphasize action-relevant interactions; aggregate graph embeddings temporally for action recognition and anticipation. Unlike prior work that uses gaze as a secondary modality, G3Ego integrates gaze into graph construction to produce concise, interpretable representations.
AI.result: On EGTEA Gaze+ and MECCANO, G3Ego achieves competitive performance against video-based approaches and consistently improves Macro-F1 under class-imbalance evaluation, while avoiding reliance on computationally expensive video pretraining.
AI.conclusion: Gaze-guided graph representations effectively capture action-relevant interactions in egocentric video, offering efficient, interpretable models that perform well without extensive video pretraining.

title: Learning When to Think: Adaptive Reasoning for Test-Time Compute Allocation
summary: Reasoning language models trained with reinforcement learning typically operate under a fixed token budget rather than an explicitly adaptive one, which can lead to over-computation on easy problems and insufficient computation on difficult ones. We study whether a model can learn to allocate its own reasoning effort by choosing, as the first token of its response, one of three modes: \textsc{NoThink} (answer as quickly as possible), \textsc{Short} (brief reasoning), or \textsc{Long} (extended reasoning). The choice is learned inside Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) with no separate router, through a shaped reward that makes each mode worthwhile at a different response length, together with hard per-mode token caps that keep the modes distinct. On a 1.5B distilled model trained on MATH, the three modes emerge without collapsing to a single choice, and the brief modes end up more accurate than \textsc{Long}, which shows that the router sorts problems by difficulty rather than at random. Averaged over three seeds, the resulting policy stays close to the base model's accuracy on the held-out MATH500 ($0.782$ vs.\ $0.796$) while cutting the mean response length from $4{,}796$ to $2{,}811$ tokens (a $41\%$ reduction). Interestingly, it also transfers to other benchmarks without retraining, with the largest savings where problems are easier, with for instance 76\% token reduction on GSM8K and at higher accuracy than the baselines at similar response length. In short, we build a reasoning model that adaptively chooses how much to reason for each problem.

AI.tldr: A reinforcement learning setup (GRPO) enables a reasoning LLM to adapt its computation budget by choosing among three modes (NoThink, Short, Long) at the first token. Per-mode token caps and a shaped reward prevent collapse to a single mode. On a 1.5B model with MATH tasks, all three modes emerge; Short is often more accurate than Long, and the policy preserves base accuracy while reducing token usage ~41%. The approach transfers to GSM8K without retraining, with larger savings on easier problems. Concludes that adaptive reasoning allocation per problem is feasible and beneficial.
AI.motivation: Fixed token budgets cause waste on easy problems and insufficient computation on hard ones. Enabling models to adaptively allocate reasoning effort could improve efficiency while maintaining or improving accuracy.
AI.method: Train a 1.5B distilled LLM with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) where the model picks the first token mode among NoThink, Short, Long (no explicit router). Apply a shaped reward to reward different response lengths and enforce hard per-mode token caps to keep modes distinct. Train on MATH; evaluate on MATH500 and GSM8K; test transfer without retraining.
AI.result: Three modes emerge without collapse to a single mode. Short mode yields higher accuracy than Long, suggesting the routing sorts problems by difficulty. Policy stays close to base model accuracy on MATH500 (0.782 vs 0.796). Mean tokens reduce from 4,796 to 2,811 (41% reduction). Transfer to GSM8K shows substantial token savings (76%) and higher accuracy than baselines at similar length.
AI.conclusion: Adaptive, per-instance reasoning budgets are learnable without a dedicated router, and can generalize across benchmarks, offering efficiency gains without sacrificing performance.

title: Exact Algebraic Computation of Learning Coefficients for Two-Dimensional Singular Models
summary: Classical information criteria such as the Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC) rely on regularity assumptions that break down for singular models, leading to incorrect model selection in settings such as deep learning. The Widely Applicable Bayesian Information Criterion (WBIC) relies on local learning coefficients $λ$, which in the analytic case coincides with local Real Log Canonical Thresholds (RLCT) of the Kullback-Leibler divergence of the model, to capture correct marginal likelihood asymptotics. Exact computation of the learning coefficients has been limited to special cases, and only sampling-based estimation methods are generally applicable. We present the first deterministic algorithm that computes local RLCTs exactly for any two-dimensional model whose Kullback-Leibler distance is contact equivalent to a polynomial, derive a bound on its complexity, and demonstrate its effectiveness for a broad class of models, with applications including polynomial neural networks. Beyond providing ground truth to calibrate sampling-based estimators, exact computation reveals algebraic structure in learning coefficients that sampling cannot and out-speeds it in the shallow regime.

AI.tldr: Introduces a deterministic algorithm to compute local RLCTs exactly for 2D models where KL distance is contact equivalent to a polynomial, with a complexity bound, enabling ground-truth calibration of estimators and revealing algebraic structure that can outperform sampling, including applications to polynomial neural networks.
AI.motivation: Regularity assumptions fail for singular models, causing BIC-based criteria to misselect models. WBIC uses local learning coefficients (λ) tied to RLCTs of the KL divergence, but exact computation is limited to special cases. A deterministic, general method for 2D models provides exact RLCTs, improving model selection for deep and polynomial networks.
AI.method: Develop a deterministic algorithm that (i) computes local RLCTs exactly for any two-dimensional model whose KL distance is contact equivalent to a polynomial; (ii) derive a bound on the algorithm's complexity; (iii) apply and demonstrate on a broad class of models, including polynomial neural networks.
AI.result: The algorithm yields exact local RLCTs for the specified class of 2D models, providing ground truth for RLCT estimation and revealing algebraic structure in learning coefficients that sampling cannot capture. It also shows faster performance than sampling in the shallow regime and demonstrates effectiveness across polynomial neural networks and related models.
AI.conclusion: This work enables exact, broadly applicable RLCT computations for singular-model learning, offering reliable calibration for WBIC and exposing underlying algebraic structure of learning coefficients, with practical benefits for model selection and understanding of shallow regimes in neural networks.

title: RoMAN-Flow: Taming Autoregressive Normalizing Flows for Offline Reinforcement Learning in Robotic Manipulation
summary: Offline reinforcement learning improves robotic policies using previously collected data without further environment interaction. Yet prevalent diffusion- and flow-matching robot policies lack tractable likelihoods, limiting their use in likelihood-based offline RL post-training. AR-NFs offer both expressive action modeling and exact likelihood evaluation, but their sequential sampling incurs substantial sampling overhead during policy optimization and deployment. We present RoMAN-Flow (Robotic Manipulation with Autoregressive Normalizing Flows), an offline reinforcement learning framework that makes AR-NF policies practical for robotic manipulation by addressing this sampling bottleneck in both stages. During policy optimization, RoMAN-Flow employs a sampling-free, advantage-weighted likelihood objective that assigns higher likelihood to high-advantage actions from the offline dataset without sampling from the autoregressive policy. For efficient deployment, it distills the optimized autoregressive policy into a one-step action generator, enabling low-latency action prediction. Experiments across multiple simulated manipulation benchmarks and real-world robotic platforms demonstrate that RoMAN-Flow achieves competitive policy performance while substantially reducing inference latency. Code is available at https://github.com/konnyaku28/RoMAN-Flow.

AI.tldr: RoMAN-Flow makes autoregressive normalizing-flow policies practical for offline RL in robotic manipulation by a sampling-free objective and one-shot distillation, achieving competitive performance with lower latency.
AI.motivation: Offline RL for robotics requires expressive, tractable policies; diffusion/flow-based methods lack tractable likelihoods; AR-NFs provide likelihoods but face sampling overhead; need efficient training and deployment.
AI.method: Use a sampling-free, advantage-weighted likelihood objective during policy optimization to prefer high-advantage (offline) actions without sampling from AR-NF; distill the trained AR-NF policy into a one-step action generator for low-latency deployment.
AI.result: Empirical results on multiple simulated manipulation benchmarks and real-world robots show competitive performance with significantly reduced inference latency; code provided.
AI.conclusion: RoMAN-Flow enables practical AR-NF offline RL for robotic manipulation by addressing sampling bottlenecks in training and deployment, offering a favorable trade-off between expressivity, likelihood evaluation, and latency.

title: Catching the Rug: Early Prediction of Fraudulent Memecoins on Solana via Machine Learning
summary: The rapid proliferation of memecoins on blockchain platforms has increased the risk of fraudulent activities, particularly rug pulls. While previous studies have focused on Ethereum-based tokens, this paper shifts the spotlight to Solana, the leading blockchain for memecoins by trading volume and token count. Unlike Ethereum, where rug pulls often exploit smart contract backdoors, Solana memecoin rug pulls are predominantly driven by liquidity manipulation and social dynamics. This research pioneers large-scale rug pull early detection in the Solana ecosystem by assembling a dataset of 6.4 million tokens over 7 months. Market analysis reveals that a vast majority of these memecoins exhibit rug pull characteristics within one hour of launch, highlighting the urgency of short-horizon prediction. Despite the absence of code-level features, we demonstrate that classic machine learning models, particularly Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), achieve robust performance in detecting potential rug pulls using only the first 5 minutes of trading data. Furthermore, we evaluate cross-platform generalization between PumpFun and Raydium, revealing that multi-source data fusion significantly mitigates domain shift and improves detection reliability. This study advances the understanding of DeFi fraud on high-throughput chains and provides a practical framework for protecting investors.

AI.tldr: Scale-focused study of rug pulls on Solana memecoins. Builds a 6.4M-token dataset over 7 months. Finds most rug pulls occur within 1 hour of launch. Demonstrates robust early detection using XGBoost with only first 5 minutes of trading data, despite no code-level features. Shows cross-platform generalization between PumpFun and Raydium improves with multi-source data fusion.
AI.motivation: Fills a gap in DeFi fraud detection on high-throughput chains like Solana, shifting focus from Ethereum backdoors to liquidity manipulation and social dynamics. Aims to deliver a practical, scalable early-warning framework for investors.
AI.method: Assembles a large-scale Solana memecoin dataset spanning 7 months and 6.4M tokens. Labels rug-pull instances based on behavioral signals (liquidity manipulation and social dynamics). Trains classical ML models, notably Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), using only the first 5 minutes of trading data. Evaluates cross-platform generalization by comparing PumpFun and Raydium, and demonstrates that multi-source data fusion mitigates domain shift and improves detection reliability.
AI.result: XGBoost yields robust detection performance with minimal temporal data. The majority of rug pulls are detected within an hour of token launch. Cross-platform evaluation shows improved reliability when fusing data from multiple sources (PumpFun and Raydium).
AI.conclusion: The study advances DeFi fraud understanding on high-throughput chains and provides a practical early-detection framework for Solana memecoins. It highlights the value of liquidity and social signals over code-level features for rug-pull detection and suggests that multi-source data fusion is key for cross-platform robustness.

title: Decoding silent reading from non-invasive EEG
comment: 45 pages (including 12 pages of Supplementary Material), 11 figures (including 2 in Supplementary Material)
summary: Non-invasive decoding of inner speech faces a fundamental data problem: a corpus pairing brain activity with a person's spontaneous inner monologue cannot be collected, and the available proxy paradigms (cued repetitive and retrospectively reported generative inner speech) are slow to acquire, poorly time-locked, and subject compliance is unverifiable. We therefore treat silent reading as a scalable proxy task and ask how much lexical and semantic information a contrastive decoder can extract from it. We report an open-vocabulary analysis of approximately 240,000 word presentations recorded from a single densely-sampled participant across 393 runs (ca. 49 h) of 19-channel dry-electrode EEG. Words from continuous narrative text were presented in rapid serial visual presentation, with typography randomised on every trial to partially decorrelate word identity from low-level visual form. A convolutional EEG encoder, optionally followed by a causal transformer, was trained with a CLIP-style contrastive objective to align short EEG windows with hidden-state embeddings of the presented word taken from a large language model. Decoding, evaluated as word-grouped top-10 retrieval against permutation baselines, was reliably above chance, extended to mid-frequency and rare words, and scaled log-linearly with training-data volume with no sign of saturation. Removing occipital and posterior-temporal electrodes reduced the word-level gain by roughly one third but left context tracking unchanged. Control analyses separate word-level decoding from narrative context tracking and from a non-neural positional prior introduced by the transformer's positional embedding. These results establish that open-vocabulary word-level information is recoverable from EEG during silent reading, and that decoding is data-limited rather than saturated.

AI.tldr: Open-vocabulary word-level decoding from EEG during silent reading using a CLIP-style objective; results show word-level information is decodable and data-limited, not saturated.
AI.motivation: Address the data bottleneck in inner-speech decoding by using silently-read text as scalable proxy task to extract lexical/semantic information from EEG.
AI.method: Convolutional EEG encoder (± optional causal transformer) trained with a CLIP-style contrastive objective to align short EEG windows with word embeddings from a large language model; dataset: ~240k word presentations in 393 runs (~49 h) across 19-channel dry EEG; rapid serial visual presentation with randomized typography; evaluations include word-grouped top-10 retrieval vs permutation baselines; control analyses separate word-level decoding from narrative context and transformer positional priors.
AI.result: Word-level information is decodable above chance; extends to mid-frequency and rare words; decoding scales log‑linearly with training data with no saturation; removing occipital/posterior-temporal electrodes reduces word-level gain by ~1/3 but context tracking remains intact.
AI.conclusion: Silent-reading EEG contains recoverable open-vocabulary lexical information; CLIP-like decoding is data-limited rather than saturated, supporting scalable approaches for decoding inner language using EEG and proxy tasks.

title: Unwarping the Lens: A Physics-Grounded Approach to Video Glasses Removal
summary: High-fidelity removal of eyeglasses from video is a major challenge in facial attribute editing, as the underlying facial geometry is often obscured by complex refractive distortions and view-dependent specular reflections. While large-scale generative priors have shown promise in eye-glasses removal via static image inpainting, they often lack the structural constraints necessary to maintain identity, expression, and pose, leading to visible "identity drift" in both static images and dynamic sequences. In this paper, we propose a novel transfer framework that addresses the stochastic nature of generative priors. Our pipeline first extracts high-fidelity synthetic face images from a commercial-grade generative model (Nano Banana, Gemini 3 Pro Image), regularizes them via a three-stage structural filtering process to preserve identity, expression, and pose, and finally applies physically-based simulation of lens optics during training to provide diverse, paired data. This process transfers Nano Banana's photo-realistic, multi-view knowledge into a specialized restoration architecture, JFSnet (Joint Feature-Spatial network). JFSnet integrates DINOv2-based semantic features with a convolutional decoder for spatial reconstruction, leveraging translation equivariance constraints to improve temporal consistency and high-frequency detail preservation. Evaluations on the curated Flickr-Faces-HQ (FFHQ) subset (12,163 images) show that our approach achieves high fidelity and structural accuracy, while maintaining inference speed of 27.68 FPS. In perceptual studies on CelebV-Text video sequences, our results are consistently preferred over diffusion and GAN-based baselines for ocular consistency, temporal stability, and overall restoration quality.

AI.tldr: Introduces JFSnet, a transfer framework for high-fidelity eyeglasses removal in video, leveraging synthetic data from a commercial generative model with three-stage structural filtering and physics-based lens optics, enabling real-time performance (27.68 FPS) and superior ocular consistency and temporal stability over baselines on FFHQ and CelebV-Text datasets.
AI.motivation: Eyeglasses removal is impeded by refractive distortions and view-dependent reflections that obscure facial geometry; existing large-scale priors cause identity drift and lack structural constraints necessary to preserve identity, expression, and pose in both images and videos.
AI.method: 1) Synthesize high-fidelity face images using a commercial generative model (Nano Banana, Gemini 3 Pro) 2) Apply a three-stage structural filtering process to preserve identity, expression, and pose 3) Train with physically-based simulation of lens optics to generate diverse, paired data 4) Transfer priors into JFSnet (Joint Feature-Spatial network) which fuses DINOv2-based semantic features with a convolutional decoder 5) Enforce translation equivariance to bolster temporal consistency and retain high-frequency detail 6) Inference at 27.68 FPS.
AI.result: On the FFHQ subset (12,163 images), the approach achieves high fidelity and structural accuracy. Perceptual studies on CelebV-Text video sequences show the method is consistently preferred over diffusion and GAN-based baselines in ocular consistency, temporal stability, and overall restoration quality.
AI.conclusion: The framework successfully transfers the generative priors to a restoration architecture, delivering accurate, temporally coherent eyeglasses removal with real-time inference and outperformance over strong baselines in both static and dynamic settings.

title: Break It Down, Pass It On: Cross-Task Skill Transfer in LLM Agents
summary: Large language model (LLM) agents can induce skills from completed tasks and reuse them later to grow more capable with experience. In practice, induced skills may transfer unreliably and can even harm the agent that retrieves them. When agent-induced skills transfer reliably across tasks remains an open question. We conduct a comprehensive and controlled study of how the way skills are induced shapes their transfer across tasks. Specifically, we compare task-level with subtask-level skill induction and text with code skill formats, the two axes along which existing methods differ. Task-level skills mostly reduce the agent's performance below its no-memory baseline while subtask-level skills raise it above on average, and text skills transfer better than code skills. To further understand our findings, we examine two complementary properties of the induced skills: specificity, which measures how closely a skill matches real tasks, and abstractness, which measures how evenly its relevance spreads across tasks. Neither property alone predicts task success, but their combined effect does, which we propose as a skill utility score. The score correlates consistently with task success when skills are transferred, and subtask-level and text skills score higher. Computing skill utility only needs the skills and task descriptions but not any task execution, so our score serves as a practical diagnostic of a skill memory before any new task runs.

AI.tldr: A controlled study shows that how skills are induced (task-level vs subtask-level) and in which format (text vs code) shape transfer; subtask-level and text skills transfer more reliably, and a 'skill utility score' combining specificity and abstractness predicts task success.
AI.motivation: To understand when induced skills transfer reliably across tasks and provide diagnostic tooling for skill memory.
AI.method: Compare four conditions (task-level text, task-level code, subtask-level text, subtask-level code); evaluate transfer performance across tasks; define specificity and abstractness; propose skill utility score; assess correlation with transfer success.
AI.result: Task-level skills often underperform the no-memory baseline; subtask-level skills outperform on average; text skills transfer better than code; neither specificity nor abstractness alone predicts success, but their combination (skill utility) correlates with transfer success; subtask-level and text skills score highest on utility.
AI.conclusion: Skill utility score is a practical diagnostic requiring only skill representations and task descriptions; favors subtask-level and text-based skill induction for more reliable transfer.

title: DICS: Data-Informed Centroid Splitting for Decision Tree Classifiers
summary: Decision tree-based models are widely used in machine learning due to their interpretability and strong empirical performance. However, training decision trees can be computationally expensive, particularly for large and high-dimensional datasets, largely due to the exhaustive search over candidate splits at each node. To improve computational efficiency, we propose Data-Informed Centroid Splitting (DICS), a clustering-based framework that constructs a compact and informative set of candidate splits using data-driven priors. By incorporating class-aware structure, DICS significantly reduces the split search space for classification tasks while preserving predictive performance. We further provide theoretical analysis showing that under the stated assumptions, DICS does not degrade the performance of classification trees compared to exhaustive split search. DICS can be incorporated into classification trees, random forests, and gradient-boosting models. Extensive experiments demonstrate that DICS achieves comparable accuracy while substantially reducing training time across synthetic and benchmark datasets, highlighting the benefit of integrating data-informed priors into split selection for scalable classification tree learning.

AI.tldr: DICS is a clustering-based framework that uses data-informed priors to generate a compact, informative set of split candidates for decision-tree learning, reducing search space without sacrificing accuracy; extends to trees, random forests, and gradient boosting; supported by theory and experiments showing speedups with comparable performance.
AI.motivation: Training decision trees is computationally expensive due to exhaustive split-search at each node, especially on large/high-dimensional data; a scalable, data-aware approach that preserves predictive performance is needed.
AI.method: Propose Data-Informed Centroid Splitting (DICS): use clustering to form a compact candidate-split set based on data-informed priors, incorporate class-aware structure, and integrate into classification trees, random forests, and gradient boosting; includes theoretical analysis showing no degradation under stated assumptions.
AI.result: DICS substantially reduces the split search space and training time while achieving comparable accuracy on synthetic and benchmark datasets; demonstrates practical scalability and efficiency.
AI.conclusion: Data-informed priors via clustering enable scalable, accurate tree-based models, enabling efficient split selection in various tree-based algorithms.

title: Prompt-Conditioned Channel Attention for Hierarchical Feature Modulation toward Anatomy-Agnostic Segmentation
summary: Anatomically plausible segmentation remains challenging because of low contrast, ambiguous boundaries, and modality-specific artifacts. Interactive segmentation has emerged as a promising strategy to guide feature extraction and improve localization, particularly in structurally ambiguous regions. However, existing methods integrate prompts through late-stage fusion and lack explicit mechanisms for prompt-driven channel-wise modulation across hierarchical feature representations, limiting their ability to capture deeper contextual and modality-specific variations. To address these limitations, we introduce Prompt-Conditioned Channel Attention (PCCA), a novel modulation mechanism that enables deep, hierarchical integration of semantic prompts within encoder-decoder networks. PCCA extracts compact channel descriptors via pooling, projects them into a shared space, and fuses them through a gated excitation mechanism to compute prompt-aware channel attention weights. These weights adaptively recalibrate feature responses across multiple network stages, enabling prompt-conditioned, semantically enriched hierarchical representations. Building on this, we propose PROMISE-Net, instantiated in two network variants: a convolutional model (PROMISE-CNN) and a transformer-based model (PROMISE-Txformer). Across the ISIC-Lesion, Kvasir-Polyp, CAMUS-Cardiac, and Kvasir-Instrument benchmarks, integrating PCCA into PROMISE-CNN yielded relative IoU gains of 10.4%, 8.7%, 0.8%, and 3.4%, respectively, over the baseline U-Net, while PROMISE-Txformer achieved corresponding gains of 7.6%, 23.0%, 2.1%, and 1.1%, respectively, over the baseline UNETR. These results show consistent improvements across architectures, imaging modalities, and anatomical targets, establishing PCCA and PROMISE-Net as a scalable, generalizable framework for prompt-aware hierarchical feature modulation in medical image segmentation.

AI.tldr: PCCA enables prompt-conditioned channel attention for hierarchical feature modulation in PROMISE-Net; achieves notable IoU gains on multiple medical segmentation benchmarks with CNN and Transformer variants.
AI.motivation: Segmentation in medical imaging is challenged by low contrast, ambiguous boundaries, and modality-specific artifacts. Existing interactive methods rely on late-stage prompt fusion and lack explicit, cross-scale, prompt-driven channel modulation.
AI.method: Introduce Prompt-Conditioned Channel Attention (PCCA) that pools channel descriptors, projects them into a shared space, and fuses them via gated excitation to compute prompt-aware channel attention weights. Integrate PCCA into encoder–decoder networks, yielding PROMISE-CNN and PROMISE-Txformer variants.
AI.result: PROMISE-CNN improves IoU by 10.4% (ISIC-Lesion), 8.7% (Kvasir-Polyp), 0.8% (CAMUS-Cardiac), 3.4% (Kvasir-Instrument) over U-Net. PROMISE-Txformer improves IoU by 7.6% (ISIC-Lesion), 23.0% (Kvasir-Polyp), 2.1% (CAMUS-Cardiac), 1.1% (Kvasir-Instrument) over UNETR.
AI.conclusion: PCCA provides scalable, generalizable prompt-aware hierarchical feature modulation for medical image segmentation, with consistent gains across architectures, modalities, and anatomical targets.

title: Phantom Gains: Auditing Self-Improvement Against a Measured Null
comment: Code and evaluation artifacts are available at https://github.com/chengxuphd/phantom-gains
summary: Whether a language model has improved itself is increasingly judged not by mean accuracy but by which individual problems it gains and loses. Tracking these transitions means differencing two noisy estimates, leaving them vulnerable to measurement artifacts. Auditing three rounds of rank-$32$ LoRA self-training on Qwen3-8B against a frozen control pushed through the identical pipeline, we identify seven measurement failures, each of which inverts a reported finding when its control is absent. Several are standard practice. A ledger built on a single greedy decode manufactures capability changes on an untrained model, largely an artifact of inference batching; the expansion statistic separating acquisition from sharpening assigns that same model a rate of $0.280$. The natural threshold repair does not survive replication: estimated across the frozen comparisons such a design already contains, its null stays non-zero. We replace it with a per-problem exact test against a pooled baseline under false-discovery-rate control, which detects nothing on any held-out replicate and is unchanged under the multiple-testing rule, error rate and pool size. Applied to a ladder of arms matched in stream, volume and evaluation, the audit finds that external distillation improves problems the base model rarely reaches while three forms of self-training do not; a regression rejects this asymmetry as a by-product of distillation's larger overall gain ($p < 10^{-8}$). On the far smaller set of problems the base model never reaches, the evidence is inconclusive, while self-training corrupts problems solved at baseline at rates well above the measured floor. Transition-level auditing therefore requires a separately measured null for every statistic it reports: nulls that cost no new experiments, built from baseline replicates a multi-arm study already owns, though not from as few as most possess.

AI.tldr: Auditing rank-32 LoRA self-training on Qwen3-8B reveals multiple measurement failures; after per-problem exact testing with FDR, most claimed transitions vanish; external distillation shows gains in hard problems while self-training does not; robust, null-per-statistic auditing is required.
AI.motivation: To disentangle true problem-level gains from artifacts in transition-level evaluation of LM self-training, ensuring effects are not driven by measurement artifacts or batching.
AI.method: Three rounds of rank-32 LoRA self-training on Qwen3-8B; compare against a frozen control through identical pipeline; identify seven measurement failures (artifacts that can invert findings without proper control); create a per-problem exact test against a pooled baseline with false-discovery-rate control; apply to a ladder of arms matched in stream, volume, and evaluation; contrast external distillation versus self-training; rely on baseline replicates for nulls.
AI.result: External distillation improves problems the base model rarely reaches; three forms of self-training do not; a regression suggests the asymmetry is due to distillation's overall gain (p < 1e-8); on the smaller set of problems the base model never reaches, evidence is inconclusive; self-training can corrupt problems solved at baseline at rates above the measured floor; suitable nulls per statistic are necessary and can be derived from baseline replicates without additional experiments.
AI.conclusion: Transition-level auditing requires a separate null for every reported statistic, constructed from baseline replicates the study already uses; without such per-statistic null controls, reported gains may be artifacts of measurement; robust auditing is feasible but often requires more stringent controls and replication to avoid spurious conclusions.

title: Dynamic Structural Causal Modeling for Sleep
summary: The causal dynamics of sleep-disordered breathing are complex and vary across patient populations, hindering the development of targeted interventions. We learn dynamic causal graphs of sleep-disordered breathing from Home Sleep Apnea Test (HSAT) recordings, revealing systematic differences in causal structure across sex and age subcohorts. We do so using the PCMCI+ algorithm on windowed fractional variables derived from 105 HSAT recordings, exploiting domain knowledge via edge blacklisting and employing bootstrap aggregation to address small subcohort sizes. The learned graphs show that temporal self-dependencies and the apnea-desaturation relationship persist across all cohorts, while other relationships vary substantially.

AI.tldr: Dynamic causal graphs of sleep-disordered breathing learned from HSAT data show sex- and age-based differences in causal structure using PCMCI+ on windowed, fractional variables; with edge blacklisting and bootstrap aggregation to cope with small subcohorts; core relationships (temporal self-dependency, apnea-desaturation) persist across cohorts while other links vary.
AI.motivation: To uncover how causal relationships in sleep-disordered breathing differ across demographic subgroups, enabling targeted interventions and better mechanistic understanding.
AI.method: Causal discovery using PCMCI+ on windowed fractional variables derived from 105 Home Sleep Apnea Test recordings. Domain knowledge incorporated via edge blacklisting; bootstrap aggregation used to stabilize inference in small subcohorts.
AI.result: The learned graphs show persistent temporal self-dependencies and apnea–desaturation links across all cohorts; other causal relationships vary substantially by sex and age subgroups.
AI.conclusion: Dynamic causal structures in sleep-disordered breathing are subgroup-dependent, supporting tailored interventions; the approach demonstrates feasibility of learning dynamic causal graphs from HSAT data with limited samples.

title: Ultra-High-Definition Restoration Transformers with Correlation Matching Transformation
summary: We propose UHDformer++, a general Transformer-based framework to solve numerous Ultra-High-Definition (UHD) image restoration tasks. UHDformer++ operates across $4$ coordinated learning spaces: 1) a high-resolution space (HR) for multi-level feature extraction, 2) a low-resolution space (LR) for learning compact, representative features, 3) a super-resolution space (SR) for upsampling low-resolution features from SR, and 4) a low-high fusion and reconstruction space (LHFR) for final image restoration. Specifically, HR extracts multi-scale high-resolution features and fuses them with low-resolution cues to produce residual images, while LR distills complementary representations from HR to improve restoration quality. To supply LHFR with richer features, SR super-resolves LR outputs before fusion. We further introduce two modules to bridge the high- and low-resolution spaces. The Feature-Refined Correlation Matching Transformation (FR-CMT) module selects the top $C/r~(C~\text{denotes the number of channels;~}r\geq1~\text{controls the squeezing level})$, from the fusion between max- and mean-pooled high-resolution features to replace less informative channels in the low-resolution Transformer. The Adaptive Channel Modulator (ACM) adaptively recalibrates multi-scale high-resolution features, ensuring that only task-relevant information propagates to LR. Extensive experiments demonstrate that UHDformer++ reduces model parameters by at least 86\% compared with recent state-of-the-art methods while achieving substantial performance gains across $5$ UHD restoration tasks, including low-light image enhancement, dehazing, deblurring, deraining, and desnowing. Code will be released at https://github.com/supersupercong/uhdformerplus.

AI.tldr: UHDformer++ is a Transformer-based framework for UHD image restoration across five tasks, integrating four learning spaces (HR, LR, SR, LHFR) and two bridging modules (FR-CMT, ACM) to achieve strong performance with significant parameter reduction.
AI.motivation: Efficient and versatile restoration of ultra-high-definition images across diverse tasks, leveraging cross-scale information while reducing model size.
AI.method: Four coordinated spaces: HR for multi-scale high-res features; LR for compact representations; SR to upsample LR outputs; LHFR for final reconstruction. FR-CMT selects top C/r channels from fused HR features to modulate LR Transformer; ACM adaptively recalibrates multi-scale HR features to feed LR. Training uses cross-space fusion and residual learning; evaluation across five UHD tasks.
AI.result: Parameter count reduced by at least 86% relative to SOTA; achieves substantial gains across five UHD restoration tasks: low-light enhancement, dehazing, deblurring, deraining, desnowing; code released.
AI.conclusion: A general, efficient Transformer-based framework for UHD restoration that generalizes across tasks with strong performance and significant parameter savings; potential for broad deployment.

title: MidTool: Mid-training Data Synthesis for Agentic Tool Use
summary: Mid-training is increasingly recognized as a critical stage for shaping the capabilities of large language models. Recent work has shown that targeted mid-training can strengthen reasoning-intensive abilities such as math and science, and can also improve agentic capabilities in software-engineering settings. In this work, we study the parallel but less explored agentic capability: general tool use. We present MidTool, an open corpus construction pipeline for agentic tool-use mid-training that combines large-scale web, PDF, and code data with synthesized supervision from real-world tool APIs, MCP skills, and document-grounded workflows. MidTool is designed to teach models how to recognize tool affordances, ground arguments from context, compose tool call workflow, and recover from incomplete information. We mid-train Qwen3-4B-Base and Qwen3-8B-Base on MidTool-Mix, and then apply follow-up post-training with both supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning. Compared with baselines, MidTool-Mix consistently improves downstream performance under both SFT and RL on BFCL, tau2-Bench, and MCP Universe. These results suggest that general tool use, like other important LLM capabilities, benefits from dedicated mid-training rather than being left entirely to post-training.

AI.tldr: Mid-training on a dedicated tool-use corpus (MidTool) improves agentic tool-use in LLMs, yielding better tool recognition, grounding, and workflow composition, with performance gains on multiple benchmarks under SFT and RL.
AI.motivation: Tool use is a key agentic capability for LLMs; mid-training offers a scalable way to instill this ability beyond post-training, by exposing models to aligned data and synthesized supervision
AI.method: Construct MidTool-Mix using large-scale web, PDFs, and code data, augmented with synthesized supervision from real-world tool APIs, MCP skills, and document-grounded workflows; mid-train Qwen3-4B-Base and Qwen3-8B-Base on MidTool-Mix; follow with supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning; evaluate on BFCL, tau2-Bench, and MCP Universe
