AI.result: MidTool-Mix yields consistent improvements over baselines in downstream tasks under both supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning across the tested benchmarks.
AI.conclusion: Dedicated mid-training for general tool use is beneficial and can shape important agentic capabilities more effectively than relying solely on post-training.

title: Physical-Support Confidence Sets for Highly Coherent Dictionaries
summary: Sparse pursuit after dictionary learning can yield a precise atom support even when its physical interpretation is not justified by the calibration data, especially for highly coherent dictionaries where alternative calibration-compatible dictionaries may assign different physical meanings to the same selected support. We develop resolution-aware physical-support inference that jointly accounts for uncertainty in the learned dictionary and in the representation of a deployment signal. Our cross-dictionary confidence correspondence retains calibration-compatible dictionaries and deployment-compatible sparse representations, then projects the surviving explanations onto physical-support space. For local coherent-atom classes with separation scale s, once the deployment data resolve the coherent-block explanation and its atom support, the minimax physical resolution from N calibration signals satisfies $δ_{\mathrm{opt}}(N,s)\asymp\min\{s,\frac{1}{\sqrt{N}s^2}\}$, with relative resolution governed by the orientation-information scale $Ns^6$. Deployment replication improves physical localization only when orientation changes cannot be absorbed by adjusting the active coefficients. For computation, we introduce active endpoint bracketing (AEB), an adaptive finite-bank procedure that evaluates only candidates that can still affect the physical report and otherwise safely coarsens or abstains. Finite-bank experiments, including a four-region synthetic application, show that a point-valued plug-in selector can be physically overprecise, whereas AEB avoids unsupported refinement with fewer candidate evaluations.

AI.tldr: Proposes resolution-aware physical-support inference for sparse pursuit post dictionary learning in highly coherent dictionaries, jointly accounting dictionary and representation uncertainty; introduces AEB adaptive pruning; derives minimax physical resolution δ_opt ≍ min{ s, 1/(√N s^2)} and orientation-information scale Ns^6; shows deployment replication improves localization only when orientation changes cannot be absorbed; finite-bank experiments show AEB reduces candidate evaluations and avoids overrefinement.
AI.motivation: When dictionaries are highly coherent, many competing explanations exist for the same support; conventional sparse pursuit can overfit to a physical interpretation not justified by calibration data. A framework is needed that preserves only physically plausible explanations across dictionaries and representations.
AI.method: Develop cross-dictionary confidence correspondence to retain calibration- and deployment-compatible explanations; project surviving explanations onto physical-support space; derive minimax physical resolution δ_opt for local coherent-atom classes with separation scale s; analyze deployment replication and orientation-scale; introduce Active Endpoint Bracketing (AEB), an adaptive finite-bank procedure that ignores candidates that cannot affect the physical report and coarsens or abstains otherwise; validate with finite-bank experiments including a four-region synthetic application.
AI.result: Theoretical results: δ_opt(N,s) asymptotically behaves as min{ s, 1/(√N s^2) }; relative resolution governed by Ns^6; deployment replication improves physical localization only when orientation variations cannot be absorbed by coefficient adjustments; AEB achieves fewer candidate evaluations while avoiding unsupported refinement; finite-bank experiments show a point-plug-in selector can be overprecise, whereas AEB is safer and more efficient.
AI.conclusion: Resolution-aware, cross-dictionary inference with AEB provides more reliable physical-support localization under dictionary uncertainty; captures interplay between calibration data, deployment data, and dictionary coherence; practical algorithm to reduce computational burden while maintaining physical validity.

title: Pandora's AI Model Routing Box: Efficient Allocation with Costly Value Estimation
summary: Heterogeneous AI systems composed of multiple models, architectures, harnesses, or inference-time settings can improve quality and efficiency by routing queries to the specialist who can answer most effectively at the lowest cost. Routing requires estimating each specialist's expected return, but this value estimation has a cost. Cheap estimators (e.g., embedding-based predictors) are fast but noisy, while accurate estimators (e.g., fine-tuned models with access to retrieval results or partial reasoning traces) are expensive. We formalize this tradeoff as an instance of Pandora's Box, the classical problem of optimal search with costly inspection. Under a Gaussian signal model, the resulting policies have closed-form value-of-information expressions that determine, for each specialist and input, whether refining the value estimate is worth its cost. We call the centralized policy Pandora's Router. We extend this to a decentralized setting, Pandora's Bidder, where specialists independently decide whether to invest in self-assessment before accepting an offered price to claim a query. Experiments across three domains---a standard multi-LLM benchmark, retrieval-augmented specialists, and LLMs with variable inference-time reasoning---show that Pandora's Router matches the routing quality of exhaustive estimation, while querying the expensive estimator far less often. In the decentralized setting, value-of-information reasoning improves allocative efficiency when competing estimates are accurate; when competing estimates are noisy, however, it can increase the strategic specialist's utility at the expense of others.

AI.tldr: A centralized and a decentralized VOI-based routing framework for heterogeneous AI specialists. Pandora's Router uses value-of-information to decide when to refine each specialist's estimated return; matches exhaustive estimation with far fewer expensive queries. Pandora's Bidder extends this to a market setting where agents decide whether to invest in self-assessment. Under Gaussian signals, closed-form VOI guides refinement.
AI.motivation: Improve quality and efficiency of heterogeneous AI systems by routing queries to the most cost-effective specialist. Estimating each specialist's value is costly; need principled tradeoffs between fast noisy estimates and accurate but expensive ones.
AI.method: Formalize routing as Pandora's Box (optimal search with costly inspection). Derive closed-form value-of-information expressions under a Gaussian signal model to decide, for each input and specialist, whether to refine the value estimate. Introduce Pandora's Router (centralized) and Pandora's Bidder (decentralized) where specialists decide on self-assessment before accepting queries. Validate with experiments on three domains: standard multi-LLM benchmark, retrieval-augmented specialists, and LLMs with variable inference-time reasoning.
AI.result: Pandora's Router achieves routing quality matching exhaustive estimation while querying expensive estimators far less often. In the decentralized setting, VOI reasoning improves allocative efficiency when competing estimates are accurate; when estimates are noisy, it can increase the strategic bidder's utility at the expense of others.
AI.conclusion: VOI-based routing provides efficient decision-making for heterogeneous AI systems: a robust centralized policy that reduces costly queries, and a decentralized policy whose performance depends on the accuracy of competing estimates and can tempt strategic behavior in noisy settings.

title: Explainable Transformer Models for Clinical Prediction Tasks on Structured Electronic Health Records
comment: Accepted at MLHC 2026; to appear in Proceedings of Machine Learning Research (PMLR)
summary: Predictive models over structured electronic health records (EHRs) remain central to machine learning for healthcare, but few have jointly emphasized quantitative laboratory information and interpretability with respect to input medical events. We present BERT-LER, a BERT-style model for coded EHR timelines pretrained and fine-tuned from a de-identified EHR dataset of 75 million patients, that encodes laboratory test results as discrete tokens while retaining graded information through percentile-based binning, paired with Integrated Gradients for token-level attributions grounded in the input EHR sequence. We benchmark our approach on the public EHRShot benchmark suite and on an asthma severity progression study based on real-world data. This addresses a methodological gap in EHR foundation-style modeling by unifying laboratory value representation and explainability in a single framework, while assessing whether both predictive performance and explanations generalize beyond standard clinical prediction tasks. Across EHRShot and asthma tasks, BERT-LER achieves predictive performance that is competitive with, and on laboratory-related tasks often exceeds, publicly available benchmark models, and provides attributions that align with clinically known risk factors. Our architecture and explainability approach can be applied to many therapeutic areas and prediction tasks using language models trained on structured EHRs.

AI.tldr: BERT-LER integrates percentile-binned lab values as discrete tokens within a BERT-like EHR model and applies Integrated Gradients for token-level explanations, achieving competitive performance and clinically meaningful attributions on EHRShot and asthma tasks.
AI.motivation: Address the gap in EHR foundation models by unifying laboratory-value representation with interpretability, and test generalization of both predictions and explanations beyond standard clinical tasks.
AI.method: Pretrain and fine-tune on a de-identified dataset of 75 million patients. Encode laboratory tests as discrete tokens via percentile-based binning to preserve graded information. Use Integrated Gradients for token-level attributions grounded in the input EHR sequence. Evaluate on EHRShot benchmarks and an asthma severity progression study.
AI.result: Predictive performance is competitive with public benchmarks; on laboratory-related tasks it often surpasses benchmarks. Attributions align with clinically known risk factors, supporting interpretability. Generalizes across the tested tasks.
AI.conclusion: The approach unifies laboratory-value representation and explainability in an EHR language-model framework and can be extended to other therapeutic areas and prediction tasks.

title: CalcSeg: Confidence-aware 3D Latent Context Curriculum Learning For Myocardial Scar Segmentation From Single-Stack LGE-CMRs
summary: Myocardial scar segmentation from single-stack late gadolinium-enhanced cardiac magnetic resonance (LGE-CMR) imaging has been a longstanding and clinically important challenge, particularly in the presence of low tissue contrast, diffuse, and small scar regions. These challenges are further intensified by the limited availability of 3D spatial context. This paper presents CalcSeg, a Confidence-aware latent context curriculum learning framework that leverages fused 3D feature representations from single-stack 2D LGE-CMR images for robust scar segmentation. Specifically, we introduce a dynamic semi-supervised curriculum learning strategy that progressively expands training from easier to more challenging scar cases using a learned confidence-aware scoring function. Such a function integrates errors in the predicted scar maps with quantified epistemic uncertainty and scar burden estimation to automatically assess sample difficulty without requiring manual labels. To compensate for the limited spatial context in single-stack acquisitions, we then develop a latent slice-wise self-attention to capture inter-slice dependencies and infer 3D spatial representations from sparse 2D inputs. We evaluate CalcSeg on multi-center clinical LGE-CMR datasets and benchmark against existing scar segmentation networks. Experimental results show that CalcSeg consistently outperforms all competing methods, particularly with substantial improvements on clinically challenging cases. Our code is released on Github.

AI.tldr: CalcSeg introduces a confidence-aware latent context curriculum learning framework for myocardial scar segmentation from single-stack LGE-CMR. It fuses 3D-like representation from 2D slices, uses a dynamic semi-supervised curriculum guided by a confidence scoring function (error, epistemic uncertainty, scar burden) to select training samples, and employs latent slice-wise self-attention to capture inter-slice context. Evaluated on multi-center data, it outperforms baselines, especially on challenging cases; code released on GitHub.
AI.motivation: Segmentation of myocardial scar from LGE-CMR is difficult due to low tissue contrast, diffuse/small scar regions, and limited 3D context when using single-stack 2D acquisitions. There is a need for methods that can synthesize 3D context and leverage unlabeled or weakly labeled data to improve robustness across centers.
AI.method: CalcSeg constructs fused 3D feature representations from single-stack 2D LGE-CMR images. It introduces a dynamic semi-supervised curriculum learning strategy that progressively exposes the model to harder scar cases via a learned confidence-aware scoring function that integrates prediction errors, epistemic uncertainty, and scar burden estimates to gauge sample difficulty. To compensate for limited spatial context, it employs latent slice-wise self-attention to capture inter-slice dependencies and infer 3D representations from sparse 2D inputs. Training leverages a curriculum from easy to hard cases with potential semi-supervised labeling (pseudo-labels/unlabeled data) guided by the confidence score.
AI.result: On multi-center clinical LGE-CMR datasets, CalcSeg consistently outperforms existing scar segmentation networks, with substantial gains on clinically challenging cases.
AI.conclusion: CalcSeg provides a robust solution for myocardial scar segmentation from single-stack LGE-CMR by fusing latent 3D context with a confidence-aware curriculum learning framework, achieving superior performance across centers. The study demonstrates the value of combining uncertainty-aware sample selection with inter-slice attention to mitigate limited 3D context in 2D acquisitions. Code is available on GitHub.

title: AI4AI-Bench: Benchmarking LLM Agents in Algorithmic Design for Recursive Self-Improvement
summary: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) asks whether an AI system can improve the process that produces AI systems, so that the next system inherits the improvement. That process is the training algorithm: a better objective or update rule improves the compute\mbox{-}capability exchange rate for every subsequent run, including the one that produces the next agent. Whether RSI is feasible therefore turns on whether an agent can design training algorithms. No benchmark isolates that ability: existing suites are won by collecting data or by tuning hyperparameters, and none tells a change to how a run is executed apart from a change to how the model learns. We present AI4AI\mbox{-}Bench, 10 frozen research repositories spanning 10 training algorithm families. In each task, an agent has 4 hours on one B300 to rewrite the training algorithm; its code is then rerun from scratch for up to 12 hours and scored by a fixed evaluator hidden from the agent, against the repository's original algorithm under the same procedure. Because the 10 metrics are incommensurable, every task is mapped onto one scale on which $0$ is an uninformative model, $0.1$ is the algorithm the repository ships, and $1.0$ is the task optimum. Across 29 configurations of 6 systems on all 10 tasks the mean score is $0.166$, and the best system reaches $0.250$: even the strongest closes under a fifth of the distance between the algorithm that was already there and the optimum. The submissions show where that distance went: most never change how the model learns at all, and the minority that do average $0.226$ against $0.126$ for the rest. More reasoning effort mostly buys the willingness to go there, taking that minority from $8\%$ of submissions to $64\%$ and the mean score from $0.094$ to $0.196$. We release the task suite, the evaluators and every scored submission, so that the measurement can be repeated as these systems change.

AI.tldr: A benchmark suite (AI4AI-Bench) to evaluate recursive self-improvement in AI training algorithms by having agents rewrite training code within fixed budgets; results show limited progress toward RSI, with most agents not altering learning, but a minority who do show modest gains. The authors release data and evaluators to enable reproducibility.
AI.motivation: To assess the feasibility of RSI by isolating the agent’s ability to redesign the training algorithm itself, which is a key bottleneck for RSI and not captured by existing benchmarks that focus on data collection or hyperparameter tuning.
AI.method: Ten frozen research repositories covering ten training-algorithm families are used. An agent gets 4 hours on a single B300 to rewrite a training algorithm; the modified code is run from scratch for up to 12 hours and scored by a fixed evaluator hidden from the agent, against the original algorithm under the same procedure. Ten tasks yield a single scale (0 to 1) per task, with 0 = uninformative model, 0.1 = repository-provided algorithm, 1.0 = task optimum. Evaluations span 29 configurations across 6 systems.
AI.result: Mean score across configurations: 0.166; best system: 0.250. Most submissions do not alter the learning process; when they do, average score is 0.226 vs 0.126 for the rest. Increasing reasoning effort raises the likelihood of changing learning, moving submissions from 8% to 64% and the mean score from 0.094 to 0.196. The authors release the task suite, evaluators, and all scored submissions for reproducibility.
AI.conclusion: The benchmark reveals that RSI-like progress is limited under the proposed setup; while some participants explore modifying the training algorithm, overall impact is modest. The dataset and evaluators enable repeatable measurement as systems evolve, providing a baseline for tracking RSI feasibility and guiding futurebenchmark design and method improvements.

title: A comparison between ceiling-mounted FMCW, IR-UWB and Wi-Fi radar for in-bedroom human activity monitoring and sleep interruption detection
comment: This paper has been submitted to IEEE Access Journal and is currently undergoing review
summary: Despite their growing importance for contact-free radio frequency (RF) based healthcare monitoring, different radio technologies such as frequency-modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radar, impulse radio ultra-wideband (IR-UWB), and Wi-Fi sensing are rarely compared under identical deployment conditions, as existing studies typically differ in hardware, datasets, and evaluation methodologies. In addition, the performance of ceiling-mounted radars, despite their practical deployment and cost advantages in healthcare environments, remain underexplored. Therefore, this paper presents a controlled comparison and analysis of ceiling-mounted FMCW, IR-UWB, and Wi-Fi sensing using synchronized recordings from 20 participants across six room layouts. All technologies are evaluated with the same convolutional neural network (CNN) on both a fine-grained 10-class human activity recognition (HAR) task and a coarse 4-class sleep monitoring task. IR-UWB achieves the highest cross-subject activity recognition performance (89.0% macro F1), while FMCW generalizes best to unseen room layouts (83.8% macro F1). For sleep monitoring, all technologies exceed 92% macro F1 in unseen environments. The results reveal a fundamental trade-off between recognition performance and environmental robustness, which can be explained through differences in range resolution, antenna diversity, Doppler resolution, and spatial information retention. These findings provide practical guidelines for the design of healthcare-oriented RF sensing systems.

AI.tldr: Controlled comparison of ceiling-mounted FMCW, IR-UWB, and Wi-Fi sensing for HAR (10-class) and sleep monitoring (4-class) using synchronized data from 20 participants in 6 rooms. IR-UWB excels in cross-subject HAR; FMCW generalizes best to unseen rooms; all tech perform well (>92% macro F1) for sleep in new environments. Trade-off noted between recognition performance and environmental robustness, linked to range/Doppler/antenna diversity and spatial information retention.
AI.motivation: There is a lack of fair, identical deployment comparisons across RF sensing modalities for healthcare monitoring, especially with ceiling-mounted devices, hindering practical deployment guidance.
AI.method: Synchronized recordings from 20 participants across six room layouts. A single convolutional neural network is used to evaluate: (i) 10-class human activity recognition, and (ii) 4-class sleep monitoring. Cross-subject evaluation and unseen-room generalization are analyzed for FMCW, IR-UWB, and Wi-Fi sensing.
AI.result: IR-UWB achieves the highest cross-subject HAR macro F1 of 89.0%. FMCW generalizes best to unseen room layouts with macro F1 of 83.8%. For sleep monitoring, all technologies exceed 92% macro F1 in unseen environments. The study attributes performance differences to range resolution, antenna diversity, Doppler resolution, and spatial information retention.
AI.conclusion: The work provides practical guidelines for RF-sensing system design in healthcare, highlighting a fundamental trade-off between recognition accuracy and environmental robustness. Designers should consider technology-specific strengths: IR-UWB for cross-subject HAR, FMCW for robustness to room changes, and all tech for stable sleep monitoring across environments.

title: DreamHand: Repurposing Video Diffusion Models for Occlusion-Robust Egocentric 3D Hand Motion Recovery
summary: Egocentric video offers scalable manipulation data for embodied AI, yet recovering metric 3D hand trajectories remains challenging due to severe object occlusion and frequent out-of-sight gaps. Existing single-frame and windowed temporal regressors fail when hand shortly leaves the frame, while recent video diffusion models (VDMs) rely on heavy, stochastic multi-step sampling as pixel-space renderers. We instead repurpose VDM into a deterministic geometry encoder. A single forward pass over the clean latent exposes scene content beyond current observations, including occluded and out-of-sight hands. We introduce DreamHand, an offline clip-level framework that extracts features via a Deterministic Clean-Latent Encoder and decodes them with a Bidirectional Spatiotemporal Decoder. DreamHand recovers continuous bimanual trajectories with metric placement and no external detector, while a Ray-Based Camera Solver supports a second configuration that needs no test-time camera intrinsics. Across five egocentric benchmarks, DreamHand sets a new state of the art, cutting MPJPE-p by 30% on occlusion-heavy ARCTIC and 40% on HOT3D. These gains reach 46%-61% once out-of-sight hands are included in the evaluation, offering a scalable path from everyday human video to robot manipulation data.

AI.tldr: DreamHand uses a deterministic latent encoder derived from a (diffusion-model) clean latent space to recover metric 3D hand trajectories from egocentric video, enabling a clip-level, detector-free, geometry-focused pipeline that outperforms baselines across five benchmarks, with intrinsics-free option via a Ray-Based Camera Solver.
AI.motivation: Egocentric video yields abundant manipulation data but recovering accurate metric 3D hand trajectories is hindered by severe occlusion and out-of-sight gaps. Single-frame/windowed regressors fail when hands leave the frame, and diffusion models incur heavy, stochastic sampling. A deterministic geometry encoder could exploit latent scene content to bridge observations.
AI.method: DreamHand operates as an offline clip-level framework. It employs a Deterministic Clean-Latent Encoder to extract latent scene features from a diffusion-model-inspired latent space, and a Bidirectional Spatiotemporal Decoder to reconstruct continuous, metric hand trajectories. A Ray-Based Camera Solver provides an intrinsics-free variant that eliminates the need for test-time camera intrinsics.
AI.result: Across five egocentric benchmarks, DreamHand achieves state-of-the-art performance, reducing MPJPE-p error by about 30% on occlusion-heavy ARCTIC and 40% on HOT3D. When including out-of-sight hands in evaluation, gains rise to 46–61%. No external hand detector is required and metric placement is achieved.
AI.conclusion: DreamHand offers a scalable, detector-free pathway from everyday egocentric video to robot manipulation data by leveraging a deterministic latent geometry encoder and a bidirectional spatiotemporal decoder, with a configurable intrinsics-free option for broader applicability.

title: An Agentic Approach for Active Data Collection, Travel Behavior Modeling, and Weather-Sensitive Demand Prediction
summary: Travel behavior research increasingly combines digital data collection with predictive modeling, yet these stages are often developed and evaluated separately. This study proposes a three-agent workflow integrating conversational data collection, structured data processing, and behavioral prediction. A chatbot-administered, image-augmented stated-preference survey collected mode choices from student commuters across five predefined weather scenarios, yielding 454 respondent-scenario observations. Weather-related associations were analyzed using a multinomial logit model, while logistic regression and random forest provided machine-learning benchmarks. Nine locally deployed large language models (LLMs), ranging from 2 to 35 billion parameters, were evaluated across four zero-shot prompt-and-context conditions and extended through persona, few-shot, and vision-based configurations. Random forest achieved 69.6% five-class accuracy, while the best text-only zero-shot LLM reached 69.9% without task-specific fitting. Habitual travel information produced the most consistent gains, Expert framing generally outperformed Role-Play, and persona information was most useful when habitual travel information was unavailable. Few-shot prompting improved prediction for several models, with gains stabilizing after a small number of examples. Using the same weather images shown to respondents, the best vision-based configuration reached 71.5% five-class accuracy, indicating that visual context may provide additional predictive information for selected models. Overall, the study shows how conversational surveys, structured data processing, conventional behavioral modeling, machine learning, and multimodal LLM prediction can be coordinated within an auditable multi-agent workflow.

AI.tldr: Integrated three-agent workflow for travel behavior prediction using conversational surveys and ML/LLMs; vision-based prompts outperform text-only in some cases; habitual-travel information and expert framing improve predictive performance; results yield ~70% five-class accuracy across models, with vision-based and LLM-based approaches offering incremental gains; demonstrates auditable multi-agent coordination of data collection, processing, and prediction.
AI.motivation: Travel-behavior studies often separate data collection from modeling, hindering auditability and integration of multimodal data. This work proposes an auditable, three-agent workflow to unify conversational data collection, structured data processing, and behavioral prediction, leveraging both traditional models and multimodal large language models.
AI.method: A three-agent workflow combined: (1) chatbot-administered, image-augmented stated-preference survey across five weather scenarios (n=454 respondent-scenario observations); (2) structured data processing with conventional modeling (multinomial logit; logistic regression; random forest); (3) evaluation of nine locally deployed large language models (2–35B) under four zero-shot prompt-and-context conditions, extended with persona, few-shot, and vision-based configurations. Weather images were used for vision prompts. Experimental comparisons included text-only LLMs and multimodal prompts.
AI.result: Random forest achieved 69.6% five-class accuracy; best text-only zero-shot LLM reached 69.9%; vision-based configuration reached 71.5% five-class accuracy. Habitual travel information produced the most consistent gains; Expert framing generally outperformed Role-Play; persona information was most useful when habitual travel information was unavailable. Few-shot prompting improved several models with gains stabilizing after a small number of examples.
AI.conclusion: The study demonstrates a feasible, auditable three-agent workflow that integrates conversational data collection, structured processing, conventional modeling, ML, and multimodal LLM prediction. Visual context can provide additional predictive power for selected models, and the arrangement of framing and prior information (habitual travel data, persona) significantly influences predictive performance.

title: Inter-X++: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Multimodal Human-Human Interaction Analysis
summary: The capability to perceive and synthesize human-human interactions is fundamental to developing intelligent digital human systems. However, existing datasets and modeling approaches are fundamentally constrained by low-fidelity kinematics, the omission of dexterous hand gestures and a severe lack of rich multimodal annotations. Furthermore, fragmented interaction representations and inconsistent evaluation protocols also impede fair and rigorous benchmarking. To systematically address these bottlenecks, we present Inter-X++, a comprehensive and large-scale benchmark designed to empower versatile HHI analysis. Captured via a novel hybrid motion capture system, Inter-X++ provides 11,388 high-fidelity interaction sequences and over 8.1M frames, featuring precise whole-body movements and detailed finger articulations. Meanwhile, we enrich the data foundation with multifaceted annotations, including hierarchical fine-grained textual descriptions, interaction categories, causal interaction orders, the relationship and personality of the subjects, as well as vertex-level contact maps and physically regularized constraints. Leveraging these elaborate annotations, we formulate a unified testing ground comprising four categories of downstream tasks that symmetrically span both generative and perceptive paradigms. To eliminate benchmarking ambiguities, we systematically standardize the interaction representations and evaluation protocols. Finally, we go beyond dataset construction to propose OpenHHI, a single and unified HHI representation and modeling framework that jointly optimizes interaction reconstruction and semantic understanding. Extensive experiments reveal that OpenHHI achieves state-of-the-art performance on both generation and perception tasks. This definitively proves that our unified representation successfully bridges interaction understanding and generation simultaneously.

AI.tldr: A large-scale, multimodal HHI benchmark Inter-X++ with a unified OpenHHI framework enabling joint generation and perception tasks and standardized evaluation.
AI.motivation: To address core limitations in existing HHI resources: low-fidelity kinematics, lack of dexterous hand gestures, insufficient multimodal annotations, fragmented interaction representations, and inconsistent benchmarking protocols.
AI.method: Inter-X++ collects 11,388 high-fidelity interaction sequences (8.1M frames) using a novel hybrid motion capture system, with rich annotations (hierarchical textual descriptions, interaction categories, causal orders, relationships/personality, vertex-level contact maps, physically regularized constraints); defines four downstream tasks spanning generative and perceptive paradigms; standardizes interaction representations and evaluation protocols; proposes OpenHHI, a unified representation and modeling framework that jointly optimizes reconstruction and semantic understanding.
AI.result: OpenHHI achieves state-of-the-art performance on both generation and perception tasks, demonstrating that the unified representation can bridge interaction understanding and generation.
AI.conclusion: Inter-X++ delivers a comprehensive benchmark for versatile HHI analysis, while OpenHHI provides a unified, end-to-end framework that unifies understanding and generation in HHI tasks, enabling robust benchmarking and research progress.

title: Swift-Image: Exploring the Performance Frontier of Compact Unified Image Generation Models
summary: We present Swift-Image, a compact unified model for text-to-image generation, single-image editing, and multi-image editing. Our goal is to explore how far a relatively small visual generator can be pushed through systematic training engineering under a constrained computational budget. Swift-Image adopts an efficient 6B single-stream DiT and a progressive training pipeline that evolves from broad semantic coverage to higher resolution, stronger visual quality, and unified generation-editing supervision. For post-training, we employ parallel expert reinforcement learning followed by multi-teacher on-policy distillation to alleviate interference among heterogeneous objectives. We further decouple high-level reasoning from pixel-level rendering with a Prompt Enhancer that translates user requests into generator-aligned visual specifications. For efficient deployment, structural pruning and few-step distillation produce 3B and accelerated variants. Swift-Image achieves leading aggregate performance among evaluated open-source models with only 6B parameters and 243K GPU training hours; the compressed 3B model incurs nearly no loss, while few-step distillation further improves aggregate editing performance with substantially fewer sampling steps. Our study also summarizes practical lessons for architecture, data curriculum, post-training, prompt enhancement, and model compression.

AI.tldr: Swift-Image is a compact 6B unified diffusion model enabling text-to-image generation and editing (single/multi-image) with a progressive training pipeline, expert RL post-training, multi-teacher distillation, and a Prompt Enhancer. It achieves leading open-source performance within 243K GPU-hours and remains highly compressible to 3B with minimal loss; the work also provides practical lessons on architecture, data curriculum, post-training, prompt design, and compression.
AI.motivation: To explore how far a compact visual generator can be pushed under constrained compute to support text-to-image generation, single-image editing, and multi-image editing in a unified model.
AI.method: Train a 6B single-stream DiT with a progressive curriculum expanding semantic coverage to high resolution and quality; apply parallel expert reinforcement learning followed by multi-teacher on-policy distillation to harmonize heterogeneous objectives; introduce a Prompt Enhancer to translate user prompts into generator-aligned visual specifications; decouple high-level reasoning from pixel-level rendering; apply structural pruning and few-step distillation to create 3B and accelerated variants; report results on open-source benchmarks using 243K GPU hours.
AI.result: Swift-Image achieves leading aggregate performance among evaluated open-source models with 6B parameters and 243K GPU hours; the compressed 3B variant incurs nearly no performance loss; few-step distillation further improves aggregate editing performance with substantially fewer sampling steps.
AI.conclusion: The work presents practical lessons across architecture, data curriculum, post-training, prompt enhancement, and model compression, demonstrating the viability of a compact, unified model for generation and editing tasks and offering scalable strategies for training and deployment.

title: 4DAnyone: Create Anyone in 4D from a Casual Monocular Video
summary: We present 4DAnyone, a framework for reconstructing 4D humans from an uncalibrated monocular video by generating reconstruction-grade multiview-consistent videos and lifting them into 4D Gaussian Splatting (4DGS). Existing camera-controlled video diffusion models synthesize plausible novel-view videos but fail to maintain consistency when scaled to the tens of target views required for 4DGS reconstruction. We identify this failure as a bounded-attention-context problem: when target views exceed the capacity of a single DiT forward pass, they must be split into groups, exposing two coupled bottlenecks. On the reference-context side, conditioning on all previously generated views grows as $O(N)$, weakening cross-view appearance guidance. On the target-context side, disjoint groups cannot directly exchange information, causing global structural drift. 4DAnyone addresses both bottlenecks with two complementary designs: Reference Context Packing (RCP) compresses growing reference views into a fixed-length mixed-resolution context with $O(1)$ reference-context complexity, while Target Context Routing (TCR) rotates target-view groupings during denoising to share context across groups at high-noise steps and stabilize details at low-noise steps. We further build the MVGameHuman dataset using our in-house game engine and combine it with light-stage and in-the-wild video datasets for training. Experiments on DNA-Rendering and DyMVHumans show that 4DAnyone outperforms prior methods in both novel-view video quality and downstream 4DGS reconstruction, with robust in-the-wild generalization. See our project page for video results and source code: https://4danyone.github.io.

AI.tldr: 4DAnyone enables reconstruction-grade 4D humans from monocular video by solving two coupled bottlenecks of bounded attention in diffusion-based multi-view synthesis via Reference Context Packing (RCP) and Target Context Routing (TCR), plus a new MVGameHuman dataset; it improves novel-view video quality and downstream 4D Gaussian Splatting reconstruction with strong in-the-wild generalization.
AI.motivation: Existing camera-controlled video diffusion models struggle to maintain cross-view consistency when the number of target views grows, due to bounded-attention-context problems. This hampers 4DGS reconstruction which requires tens of views.
AI.method: Introduce Reference Context Packing (RCP) to compress growing reference views into a fixed-length context with O(1) complexity, and Target Context Routing (TCR) to rotate target-view groupings so information exchanges occur across groups at high-noise steps and stabilize details at low-noise steps. Build MVGameHuman dataset and train on it plus light-stage and in-the-wild data.
AI.result: 4DAnyone outperforms prior methods in both novel-view video quality and downstream 4DGS reconstruction, with robust generalization to in-the-wild data.
AI.conclusion: The proposed RCP and TCR designs effectively address bounded-attention-context bottlenecks, enabling scalable, consistent 4D reconstruction from uncalibrated monocular video; the MVGameHuman dataset supports training and demonstrates practical performance gains.

title: WithEveryone: Unified Planning and Identity Grounding for Group Image Generation
comment: Project Page: doby-xu.github.io/WithEveryone/ ;Code will be released: github.com/Doby-Xu/WithEveryone/
summary: Identity-preserving image generation becomes increasingly unreliable when a scene must contain many specified people. Beyond retaining each identity, the model must bind every reference to a distinct person and location, while training-time identity losses must establish correspondence among several noisy predicted faces. We introduce WithEveryone, a unified framework for generating group images up to ten reference identities. WithEveryone injects each selected identity as an addressed token, predicts a structured identity--layout plan, and renders the plan as a visual condition. Its key objective, Layout-Grounded ID Loss, uses annotated face regions to supervise the intended identities directly, avoiding unstable embedding-based face matching; ID Representation Forcing additionally trains a prediction for each identity before image synthesis. On an identity-disjoint benchmark, WithEveryone achieves the highest target-context identity similarity, improving face similarity from 0.462 for GPT-Image-2 to 0.499, while reducing copy-paste artifacts from 0.169 to 0.055. It further covers 97.3\% of the requested identities with a duplicate rate of only 2.8\%. These results show that explicit identity--layout grounding enables identity-preserving generation to scale to larger groups without relying on direct reference-face copying.

AI.tldr: WithEveryone is a framework for generating group images with up to ten identities by grounding identities to a layout via an identity-layout plan and Layout-Grounded ID Loss, improving identity preservation and reducing copy-paste artifacts.
AI.motivation: Scaling identity-preserving image generation to multi-person scenes requires binding multiple reference identities to distinct people and locations while handling noisy predicted faces; existing methods struggle with stable identity matching and layout-consistent rendering.
AI.method: Injects each selected identity as an addressed token, predicts a structured identity–layout plan, and renders the plan as a visual condition. Introduces Layout-Grounded ID Loss to supervise intended identities directly using annotated face regions rather than embedding-based face matching. Also proposes ID Representation Forcing to train a per-identity predictor before synthesis.
AI.result: On an identity-disjoint benchmark, WithEveryone achieves the highest target-context identity similarity (0.499, up from 0.462 with GPT-Image-2) and reduces copy-paste artifacts (0.055, down from 0.169). It covers 97.3% of requested identities with a 2.8% duplicate rate.
AI.conclusion: Explicit identity–layout grounding enables scalable, identity-preserving group image generation without relying on direct reference-face copying.
